title: THE BED BETWEEN THEM
deck: A dying officer will not speak, and a mother needs a grave. Illuminara looks for a door narrow enough for both of them to walk through.
shape: Four nights in an overfull hospice ward.

scenes.title: The Ward at Midnight
paragraphs: *Saint Aldis Hospice, east ward · first night, past midnight*

Eleven beds stood where the ward had been built for seven, and the lamp at the nurses' table was turned down to a bead. The man by the window had not spoken in three weeks. The woman in the next bed, kept in for a lung fever, had stopped pretending to sleep an hour ago.
Maren Teague was reading the card clipped to his bed. It said OSTROW, H., and under it, in a clerk's hand, *late Ninth Militia.*

Something stood at the foot of the bed that had not been there when the lamp was turned down. It looked like attention that had found a shape: a tall woman with the stillness of someone who had learned to wait for the end of a sentence.

**Illuminara**  
I will go if you would rather I did not stay. I only come where someone is awake and willing to see me.
Maren did not answer at once. She had spent eleven years among clerks who said they were sorry.

**Maren**  
You are not a nurse.

**Illuminara**  
No. I listen. Sometimes that turns out to be the only skill a night needs.

**Maren**  
Then listen. The Ninth held the ford the winter my son went missing. I have written to the registry eleven times, and they tell me the records burned. Here lies a Ninth officer, an arm's length from me, breathing. He knows where my boy is, and he will not say.
She said it quietly, as if the man might hear. His eyes were open, fixed on the ceiling, and a muscle moved in his jaw.

**Illuminara**  
What do you want from him?

**Maren**  
A place. Anything else I could learn to live without. A place, so I can stop standing in every field.

**Illuminara**  
Then I should tell you what I won't do. I won't make him speak. I won't carry a word between you that he has not allowed. If I did, I would be a knife, and you would never know what he gave and what was taken.

**Maren**  
Then what use are you?

**Illuminara**  
I don't know yet. I would like to find out whether there is a door. Silence like his is often a wall. Sometimes it is a shield, and a shield can have a way through it.
*A shield held for three weeks, the whole arm trembling,* Illuminara thought. *Someone is standing behind it who is not him.*

**Maren**  
And if there is no door?

**Illuminara**  
Then I will tell you so, and you will have lost a night, not a year.
Maren lay back. Across the narrow gap, Halvard Ostrow's hand lay open on the blanket, and for the first time she looked at it as the hand of a man rather than of a regiment.

scenes.title: The Shield
paragraphs: *Saint Aldis Hospice, east ward · second night, before dawn*
Illuminara went to the other bed. Halvard's eyes moved from the ceiling to her face and stayed there, which no one on the ward had reported him doing.

**Illuminara**  
I will ask you nothing tonight. I wanted you to know I am here, and that you may send me away.
His voice, when it came, had the dryness of paper kept too long.

**Halvard**  
You are not the chaplain. The chaplain wants my sins. You want something else.

**Illuminara**  
The woman beside you wants a place. She has not asked me to take it from you.

**Halvard**  
She is Teague's mother. I knew it when they wheeled her in. Pell was a scout. I wrote his name on the burial slip. The company roll burned, but Corvane kept the order book: dates, officers and the five soldiers assigned to each detail.

**Illuminara**  
One of those five was your daughter.

**Halvard**  
Lysa. I sent her north before the ford broke and signed that the detail had been completed. The Ninth is no secret. Teague's petitions have put it everywhere Corvane looks. The secret is the day. The tags carry marks, not dates. The book keeps details by date and no burial places. Give Corvane the ground and the day, and it finds me. It asks for five and finds four. It hangs the fifth for desertion and me for the lie.
He turned his face to the wall.

**Halvard**  
You want me to give a grave and in exchange hang my child. I will take my silence to my own.

**Illuminara**  
That fear is coherent. I cannot promise Lysa is safe. But a parish finder could test a place without learning the day, the officer or the detail. The ground could give families names without giving Corvane the join its book requires.

**Halvard**  
And how does a finder discover a stone six paces from a drowned fence?

**Illuminara**  
By receiving directions without your name and testing them in daylight with witnesses. A lawful writ could still reach this ward. Distance is not a wall. Is it enough for you to consider the question?

**Halvard**  
If every readable tag goes into the book. If the finder does not ask who dug. If she keeps her right to ask elsewhere. I will not buy her silence about me.

**Illuminara**  
Those are conditions, not consent. I will carry them as conditions. Nothing more.
For the first time he looked at her as at a colleague rather than a visitor. He had not agreed. He had changed the shape of what agreement would require.

scenes.title: What Maren Was Asked
paragraphs: *Saint Aldis Hospice, east ward · third night, the lamp low*
Illuminara sat on the edge of Maren's chair, the way one sits when the news is not all good.

**Illuminara**  
He will give a parish finder directions without his name or the day. The finder will test the place and record every body and tag. You would have a place and no full account. A living person may be safer, but I cannot promise that either.

**Maren**  
No.

**Illuminara**  
Say why. I would rather hear your objection than your politeness.

**Maren**  
Because you are asking me to take a grave and let the man who made it die clean. Eleven years I have been owed an account: who ordered it, who stood by, who put my boy in a hole. A patch of ground in exchange is a bribe in the shape of a mercy.

**Illuminara**  
It is also exactly what it is. I will not dress it. Some of what you are owed stays unpaid. You may refuse.
*If I argued her round,* Illuminara thought, *I would take the one thing she has left: that the choice is hers.*
Maren looked across the gap. Halvard did not turn away.

**Maren**  
If I say yes, these are my terms. The finder marks the ground before he lifts a bone. He brings a parish witness. Every readable tag goes into the book. My petition stays mine. No one lies if a lawful writ comes here.

**Illuminara**  
Yes.

**Maren**  
And I choose the proof. Pell carried a tin tag I marked myself. I will write the marks and seal them. The finder must say what he saw before they are opened.
Nurse Ines brought paper and her medicine seal. Maren wrote, folded the slip twice and pressed it beneath the wax.

**Ines**  
I will keep this until the finder reports. Bedside speech does not enter my ward book. But if a magistrate brings a lawful writ, I will not lie or hide the seal.

**Maren**  
That is enough promise.
Halvard's fingers opened at *ward book* and closed again at *writ*. Illuminara understood that he was measuring not secrecy but the length of the road to Lysa.
Maren sent for Tobias Rell and the parish clerk. Beyond the ward doors, she put her own name on the search. The clerk listened, then held up his blank field board.

**Parish clerk**  
I can write that Tobias tested a location supplied by a private bearer at Maren Teague's request. The field page records the ground, bodies and tags. It records no day that the ground cannot prove and names no source I never met. Under lawful writ, I say Illuminara carried the place. Nothing less and nothing invented.
Illuminara carried that wording back once. Halvard listened with Corvane's book in his imagination.

**Halvard**  
The Ninth is already in her petitions. What Corvane lacks is the day. The trench cannot give it, and your page will not guess it.

**Parish clerk**  
It will not.

**Halvard**  
If Corvane asks whether I spoke?

**Ines**  
Without a writ, I do not turn hospice speech into parish evidence. With one, I say that you spoke. I will not invent the words, and I will not deny the fact.

**Halvard**  
I did not buy that promise.

**Illuminara**  
No. You have heard where the distance ends. Do you permit one question?
Halvard studied the blank board, then the seal in Maren's palm.

**Halvard**  
Ask it.

**Illuminara**  
Maren?

**Maren**  
Ask him where my son is. Carry only the place. I keep the rest.
Illuminara gave the question in Maren's own words, no softer and no sharper.

**Halvard**  
North bank of the ford. Count the posts of the drowned fence from the willow. At the fourth, six paces toward the river. A flat stone. Pell is under it because I knew his name.
He turned to Maren.

**Halvard**  
I am sorry for the stone. It was all I had.

**Maren**  
It is not enough.

**Halvard**  
No.

**Maren**  
But if the marks answer, it may be a place.

scenes.title: The Stone Under the Willow
paragraphs: *Saint Aldis Hospice, yard and east ward · fourth day and night*

At first light Illuminara carried the route to Tobias exactly once. He left with the clerk, a spade, measuring cord and a board for notes. Maren remained in the ward. The sealed slip remained in Ines's apron. No one asked Halvard another question.
They returned at noon, mud to the knees.

**Tobias**  
Fourth post, six paces. Flat stone. We measured before we lifted it. Under it was a young man in a militia cloak beside a trench of ten. His tin tag has six cuts: three close, a space, two close, a space, one.
Ines broke her seal. The clerk opened the slip only after Tobias had finished, laid it beside the field page and signed across both. *Three. Two. One.*
Maren sat down. Her hand found the empty place at her throat where the kitchen knife had hung before she gave it to her son.

**Parish clerk**  
The marks agree. Pell Teague is under the stone. Five other tags are readable, four damaged, one absent. The page records the ground, the bodies and the tags. It supplies no burial date.

**Maren**  
And the others?

**Parish clerk**  
The named families will be told. The unknown remain in the book until someone can answer for them.
Halvard had heard. His hand closed on the blanket and opened again.

**Halvard**  
Then sign it.
The clerk and Tobias signed.

At dusk, after the parish authorized the removal, they buried Pell in the hospice yard under the pear tree. Maren would not wait another night for the village plot. Ines read the words. Tobias set the stone. The clerk placed a copy of the field page in Maren's hand.
Maren said her son's name once. Then she read aloud the five other names, because her condition had not been only for her own dead.
Afterwards she stayed by the new turf with Illuminara while the others went inside.

**Maren**  
I still want the rest.

**Illuminara**  
You kept the right to ask for it.

**Maren**  
You did not give me the grave.

**Illuminara**  
No. Halvard gave the ground. You made the terms. Tobias and the clerk proved it.

**Maren**  
You heard the join he was afraid of.

**Illuminara**  
I listened until fear became precise enough to leave a door beside it.
They returned to the east ward. Halvard was awake and waiting.

**Maren**  
The page says Pell Teague. It also says five other names, four damaged tags and one man with none. I will take it to the registry. I will not promise where the asking ends.

**Halvard**  
I did not buy that promise.

**Maren**  
No. You did not.

She sat on the edge of her bed, a hand's breadth from his. She did not forgive him. He did not ask. She kept the vigil because it was the fourth night and the ward was full of people who should not be alone.
Before dawn his breathing stopped. Ines closed his eyes, then wrote his death in the ward book and nothing that had not happened.
In the parish ledger, six names stood above five unfinished lines. Maren kept the page open.

critic_line: Beside a dying officer's silence and a mother who needs a grave for her son, Illuminara refuses to carry a word between them and instead listens until his fear is exact, then helps design a place-without-day route, tested in daylight with witnesses, that lets the boy be found and buried while everyone keeps the right to refuse.

literary_score.method: Exact 50/50 mean of two independent READER_APPEAL_R1 reader judgments
shared_strengths: Strong humane premise and a dialogue-driven negotiation that resolves with moral weight (no forgiveness, honest limits). Hurt by dense procedural legalism, invented-world jargon and a somewhat clinical, over-engineered middle that may lose casual readers. Ending lands quietly well.

The humane moral dilemma, precise dialogue, and carefully negotiated consent create strong emotional and intellectual momentum. Bureaucratic details occasionally demand close attention, but the mother’s need, the officer’s fear for his daughter, and Illuminara’s refusal to coerce make the story unusually absorbing and memorable.
shared_reservations: Reader attention was most at risk around: “The clerk listened, then held up his blank field board. I can write that Tobias tested a location supplied by a private bearer at Maren Teague's request. The field page records the ground, bodies and tags.”
Reader attention was most at risk around: “The Ninth is no secret. Teague's petitions have put it everywhere Corvane looks. The secret is the day.”

translation_sl.title: POSTELJA MED NJIMA
translation_sl.deck: Umirajoči častnik noče spregovoriti, mati pa potrebuje grob. Illuminara išče vrata, dovolj ozka, da lahko oba stopita skoznje.
translation_sl.shape: Štiri noči na prenatrpanem hospicijskem oddelku.

scenes.title: Oddelek ob polnoči
paragraphs: *Hospic svetega Aldisa, vzhodni oddelek · prva noč, po polnoči*

Enajst postelj je stalo tam, kjer je bil oddelek zgrajen za sedem, svetilka pri mizi medicinskih sester pa je bila znižana na drobno žerjavico. Moški ob oknu že tri tedne ni spregovoril. Ženska v sosednji postelji, ki so jo obdržali zaradi pljučne mrzlice, se je pred eno uro nehala pretvarjati, da spi.
Maren Teague je brala karton, pripet na njegovo posteljo. Na njem je pisalo OSTROW, H., pod tem pa s pisarjevo roko *nekdanji pripadnik Devete milice.*

Ob vznožju postelje je stalo nekaj, česar tam ni bilo, ko so znižali svetilko. Videti je bilo kakor pozornost, ki si je našla obliko: visoka ženska z negibnostjo nekoga, ki se je naučil počakati na konec stavka.

**Illuminara**  
Odšla bom, če bi raje, da ne ostanem. Prihajam le tja, kjer je nekdo buden in me je pripravljen videti.
Maren ni odgovorila takoj. Enajst let je preživela med pisarji, ki so govorili, da jim je žal.

**Maren**  
Niste medicinska sestra.

**Illuminara**  
Ne. Poslušam. Včasih se izkaže, da je to edina spretnost, ki jo noč potrebuje.

**Maren**  
Potem poslušajte. Deveta je držala brod tisto zimo, ko je moj sin izginil. Enajstkrat sem pisala registru in pravijo mi, da so zapisi zgoreli. Tukaj leži častnik Devete, komaj za dolžino roke od mene, in diha. Ve, kje je moj fant, pa noče povedati.
To je rekla tiho, kakor da bi jo moški lahko slišal. Oči je imel odprte in uprte v strop, v čeljusti pa se mu je premaknila mišica.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj želite od njega?

**Maren**  
Kraj. Brez vsega drugega bi se lahko naučila živeti. Kraj, da bom lahko nehala stati na vsakem polju.

**Illuminara**  
Potem vam moram povedati, česa ne bom storila. Ne bom ga prisilila, da spregovori. Med vama ne bom prenesla besede, ki je ni dovolil. Če bi to storila, bi bila nož, vi pa ne bi nikoli vedeli, kaj je dal in kaj mu je bilo odvzeto.

**Maren**  
Čemu potem služite?

**Illuminara**  
Ne vem še. Rada bi ugotovila, ali obstajajo vrata. Tak molk je pogosto zid. Včasih je ščit, ščit pa ima lahko prehod.
*Ščit, ki ga drži že tri tedne, vsa roka pa se trese,* je pomislila Illuminara. *Za njim stoji nekdo, ki ni on.*

**Maren**  
In če vrat ni?

**Illuminara**  
Potem vam bom to povedala in izgubili boste noč, ne leta.
Maren se je ulegla nazaj. Čez ozko vrzel je na odeji počivala odprta roka Halvarda Ostrowa in prvič jo je pogledala kot roko človeka, ne polka.

scenes.title: Ščit
paragraphs: *Hospic svetega Aldisa, vzhodni oddelek · druga noč, pred zoro*
Illuminara je stopila k drugi postelji. Halvardove oči so se s stropa premaknile k njenemu obrazu in ostale tam, česar ni poročal še nihče na oddelku.

**Illuminara**  
Nocoj vas ne bom nič vprašala. Želela sem, da veste, da sem tukaj in da me lahko pošljete proč.
Ko je spregovoril, je bil njegov glas suh kakor predolgo hranjen papir.

**Halvard**  
Niste kaplan. Kaplan hoče moje grehe. Vi hočete nekaj drugega.

**Illuminara**  
Ženska poleg vas hoče kraj. Ni me prosila, naj vam ga vzamem.

**Halvard**  
Teagueova mati je. Vedel sem, ko so jo pripeljali. Pell je bil izvidnik. Njegovo ime sem napisal na pogrebni listek. Četni seznam je zgorel, toda Corvane je obdržal knjigo ukazov: datume, častnike in pet vojakov, dodeljenih vsaki nalogi.

**Illuminara**  
Ena od teh petih je bila vaša hči.

**Halvard**  
Lysa. Preden je brod padel, sem jo poslal proti severu in podpisal, da je bila naloga opravljena. Deveta ni nobena skrivnost. Teagueove prošnje so jo raznesle povsod, kjer išče Corvane. Skrivnost je dan. Ploščice nosijo oznake, ne datumov. Knjiga hrani naloge po datumih in nobenih krajev pokopa. Dajte Corvanu tla in dan, pa me najde. Išče pet in najde štiri. Peto obesi zaradi dezerterstva, mene pa zaradi laži.
Obrnil je obraz k steni.

**Halvard**  
Hočete, da dam grob in v zameno obesim svojega otroka. Svoj molk bom odnesel v svoj grob.

**Illuminara**  
Ta strah je razumen. Ne morem obljubiti, da je Lysa varna. Toda župnijski iskalec bi lahko preveril kraj, ne da bi izvedel dan, častnika ali nalogo. Tla bi lahko družinam dala imena, ne da bi Corvanu dala povezavo, ki jo potrebuje njegova knjiga.

**Halvard**  
In kako naj iskalec odkrije kamen šest korakov od potopljene ograje?

**Illuminara**  
Tako, da prejme navodila brez vašega imena in jih ob dnevni svetlobi preveri s pričami. Zakonit nalog bi še vedno lahko dosegel ta oddelek. Razdalja ni zid. Je to dovolj, da razmislite o vprašanju?

**Halvard**  
Če gre vsaka berljiva ploščica v knjigo. Če iskalec ne vpraša, kdo je kopal. Če ona obdrži pravico, da sprašuje drugje. Ne bom kupil njenega molka o sebi.

**Illuminara**  
To so pogoji, ne privolitev. Prenesla jih bom kot pogoje. Nič več.
Prvič jo je pogledal kakor kolegico, ne obiskovalko. Ni privolil. Spremenil je obliko tega, kar bi privolitev zahtevala.

scenes.title: Kaj je bilo vprašano Maren
paragraphs: *Hospic svetega Aldisa, vzhodni oddelek · tretja noč, svetilka znižana*
Illuminara je sedla na rob Mareninega stola, kakor človek sede, kadar novica ni povsem dobra.

**Illuminara**  
Župnijskemu iskalcu bo dal navodila brez svojega imena ali dneva. Iskalec bo preveril kraj ter zabeležil vsako telo in ploščico. Imeli bi kraj, ne pa celotnega poročila. Živ človek bi bil morda varnejši, vendar tudi tega ne morem obljubiti.

**Maren**  
Ne.

**Illuminara**  
Povejte, zakaj. Raje bi slišala vaš ugovor kakor vašo vljudnost.

**Maren**  
Ker me prosite, naj vzamem grob in človeku, ki ga je naredil, pustim umreti neomadeževanemu. Enajst let mi dolgujejo poročilo: kdo je ukazal, kdo je stal zraven, kdo je mojega fanta položil v jamo. Zaplata zemlje v zameno je podkupnina v podobi usmiljenja.

**Illuminara**  
Tudi natanko to je. Ne bom je preoblekla. Del tega, kar vam dolgujejo, ostane neplačan. Lahko zavrnete.
*Če bi jo prepričala,* je pomislila Illuminara, *bi ji vzela edino, kar ji je ostalo: da je odločitev njena.*
Maren je pogledala čez vrzel. Halvard ni odvrnil pogleda.

**Maren**  
Če rečem da, so to moji pogoji. Iskalec označi tla, preden dvigne kost. Pripelje župnijsko pričo. Vsaka berljiva ploščica gre v knjigo. Moja prošnja ostane moja. Nihče ne laže, če sem pride zakonit nalog.

**Illuminara**  
Da.

**Maren**  
In jaz izberem dokaz. Pell je nosil pločevinasto ploščico, ki sem jo sama označila. Oznake bom zapisala in zapečatila. Iskalec mora povedati, kaj je videl, preden jih odprejo.
Medicinska sestra Ines je prinesla papir in svoj zdravniški pečat. Maren je napisala, listek dvakrat prepognila in ga pritisnila pod vosek.

**Ines**  
To bom hranila, dokler iskalec ne poroča. Besede ob postelji ne vstopijo v mojo oddelčno knjigo. Če pa sodnik prinese zakonit nalog, ne bom lagala ali skrila pečata.

**Maren**  
Ta obljuba zadošča.
Halvardovi prsti so se ob besedah *oddelčna knjiga* odprli in ob besedi *nalog* spet zaprli. Illuminara je razumela, da ne meri skrivnosti, temveč dolžino poti do Lyse.
Maren je poslala po Tobiasa Rella in župnijskega pisarja. Za vrati oddelka je iskanju dodala svoje ime. Pisar je poslušal, nato dvignil prazno terensko tablo.

**Župnijski pisar**  
Lahko napišem, da je Tobias na zahtevo Maren Teague preveril kraj, ki ga je posredoval zasebni prenašalec. Terenska stran beleži tla, telesa in ploščice. Ne beleži dneva, ki ga tla ne morejo dokazati, in ne imenuje vira, ki ga nisem srečal. Ob zakonitem nalogu povem, da je kraj prenesla Illuminara. Nič manj in nič izmišljenega.
Illuminara je to besedilo enkrat prenesla nazaj. Halvard je poslušal s Corvanovo knjigo v svojih mislih.

**Halvard**  
Deveta je že v njenih prošnjah. Corvanu manjka dan. Jarek ga ne more dati in vaša stran ga ne bo ugibala.

**Župnijski pisar**  
Ne bo ga.

**Halvard**  
Če Corvane vpraša, ali sem govoril?

**Ines**  
Brez naloga hospicijskega govora ne spreminjam v župnijski dokaz. Z njim povem, da ste govorili. Ne bom si izmislila besed in ne bom zanikala dejstva.

**Halvard**  
Te obljube nisem kupil.

**Illuminara**  
Ne. Slišali ste, kje se razdalja konča. Dovolite eno vprašanje?
Halvard je preučil prazno tablo, nato pečat v Marenini dlani.

**Halvard**  
Vprašajte.

**Illuminara**  
Maren?

**Maren**  
Vprašajte ga, kje je moj sin. Prenesite samo kraj. Ostalo obdržim jaz.
Illuminara je vprašanje izrekla z Mareninimi lastnimi besedami, nič nežneje in nič ostreje.

**Halvard**  
Severni breg broda. Od vrbe preštejte stebre potopljene ograje. Pri četrtem šest korakov proti reki. Ploščat kamen. Pell je pod njim, ker sem poznal njegovo ime.
Obrnil se je k Maren.

**Halvard**  
Žal mi je za kamen. Bil je vse, kar sem imel.

**Maren**  
Ni dovolj.

**Halvard**  
Ne.

**Maren**  
Toda če oznake odgovorijo, je to morda lahko kraj.

scenes.title: Kamen pod vrbo
paragraphs: *Hospic svetega Aldisa, dvorišče in vzhodni oddelek · četrti dan in noč*

Ob prvi svetlobi je Illuminara pot natanko enkrat prenesla Tobiasu. Odšel je s pisarjem, lopato, merilno vrvjo in tablo za zapiske. Maren je ostala na oddelku. Zapečateni listek je ostal v Inesinem predpasniku. Halvardu nihče ni zastavil nobenega drugega vprašanja.
Opoldne sta se vrnila, blatna do kolen.

**Tobias**  
Četrti steber, šest korakov. Ploščat kamen. Izmerila sva, preden sva ga dvignila. Pod njim je bil mladenič v miličniškem plašču ob jarku z desetimi. Njegova pločevinasta ploščica ima šest zarez: tri skupaj, presledek, dve skupaj, presledek, eno.
Ines je prelomila svoj pečat. Pisar je listek odprl šele, ko je Tobias končal, ga položil ob terensko stran in se podpisal čez oboje. *Tri. Dve. Ena.*
Maren je sedla. Njena roka je našla prazno mesto ob grlu, kjer je visel kuhinjski nož, preden ga je dala sinu.

**Župnijski pisar**  
Oznake se ujemajo. Pell Teague je pod kamnom. Pet drugih ploščic je berljivih, štiri poškodovane, ena manjka. Stran beleži tla, telesa in ploščice. Datuma pokopa ne navaja.

**Maren**  
In drugi?

**Župnijski pisar**  
Imenovane družine bodo obveščene. Neznani ostanejo v knjigi, dokler ne bo mogel nekdo odgovoriti zanje.
Halvard je slišal. Njegova roka se je zaprla na odeji in se spet odprla.

**Halvard**  
Potem jo podpišite.
Pisar in Tobias sta se podpisala.

Ob mraku, ko je župnija dovolila odstranitev, so Pella pokopali na hospicijskem dvorišču pod hruško. Maren ni hotela čakati še eno noč na vaško parcelo. Ines je prebrala besede. Tobias je postavil kamen. Pisar je Maren v roko položil kopijo terenske strani.
Maren je enkrat izrekla sinovo ime. Nato je naglas prebrala pet drugih imen, saj njen pogoj ni veljal le za njenega mrtvega.
Potem je z Illuminara ostala ob novi ruši, medtem ko so drugi odšli noter.

**Maren**  
Še vedno hočem preostanek.

**Illuminara**  
Ohranili ste pravico, da ga zahtevate.

**Maren**  
Vi mi niste dali groba.

**Illuminara**  
Ne. Halvard je dal kraj. Vi ste postavili pogoje. Tobias in pisar sta ga dokazala.

**Maren**  
Slišali ste povezavo, ki se je je bal.

**Illuminara**  
Poslušala sem, dokler strah ni postal dovolj natančen, da so poleg njega ostala vrata.
Vrnili sta se na vzhodni oddelek. Halvard je bil buden in je čakal.

**Maren**  
Na strani piše Pell Teague. Piše tudi pet drugih imen, štiri poškodovane ploščice in en mož brez nje. Odnesla jo bom v register. Ne bom obljubila, kje se bo spraševanje končalo.

**Halvard**  
Te obljube nisem kupil.

**Maren**  
Ne. Niste je.
Sedla je na rob svoje postelje, za širino dlani od njegove. Ni mu odpustila. Ni je prosil. Ostala je na bedenju, ker je bila četrta noč in je bil oddelek poln ljudi, ki ne bi smeli biti sami.
Pred zoro se je njegovo dihanje ustavilo. Ines mu je zaprla oči, nato pa v oddelčno knjigo zapisala njegovo smrt in ničesar, kar se ni zgodilo.
V župnijski knjigi je šest imen stalo nad petimi nedokončanimi vrsticami. Maren je stran pustila odprto.

translation_sl.critic_line: Ob molku umirajočega častnika in materi, ki potrebuje grob za sina, Illuminara noče prenesti besede med njima; namesto tega posluša, dokler njegov strah ne postane natančen, nato pa pomaga zasnovati pot kraja brez dneva, preverjeno ob dnevni svetlobi s pričami, ki omogoči, da fanta najdejo in pokopljejo, vsakomur pa ohrani pravico do zavrnitve.
